7921645569005257804:
Zhenming Year 3, March 7th
First time leaving the mountains. The Elder commanded me to earn fifty taels of silver.
...Fifty taels! It would take a family of three years of hard labor to save that much. Quite distressing.
Zhenming Year 3, March 8th
Encountered bandits on the road, confiscated one tael and three maces.

Zhenming Year 3, March 9th
Encountered bandits again, confiscated two taels and two maces.

Zhenming Year 3, March 10th
Another run-in with bandits, seized seven taels and eight maces.

Zhenming Year 3, March 11th
Three bandit encounters in a single day! Alas! The chaos of the world leaves me sighing in despair.

Zhenming Year 3, March 12th
More bandits. Counted my silver—already over twenty taels, nearly halfway to fifty.
Perhaps I should seek out more bandits... No, no. As a disciple of the Mo Gate, how could I stoop to plundering?
Zhenming Year 3, March 13th
Stumbled upon bandits by chance, gained three taels. They’re like ants—unavoidable. Not my fault.

Zhenming Year 3, March 14th
Met Khitan horse bandits raiding within the pass, laden with riches. Confiscated forty-nine taels of silver!
Grieved—was all my training truly useless?
Zhenming Year 3, March 15th
Found several Khitan horse bandits, took twenty taels. Spat at them—pathetic.

Zhenming Year 3, March 16th
Couldn’t find any Khitan horse bandits? Sighed, "I’ve fallen."

Zhenming Year 3, March 17th
Reached the Hutuo River, saw a hundred horses stampeding, a thousand bows twanging—Khitan bandits ambushing three Swordsmen.
Excellent! This time, I’ll surely seize over a hundred taels!
Zhenming Year 3, March 18th
Finally, my skills proved useful. Those three Swordsmen paid me fifty taels to build a bridge over the Hutuo River.
Zhenming Year 3, March 19th
Learned today the three Swordsmen were named Xu Zhigao, Wang Qing, and Li Wuxin.
Troubling—the Mo Gate stays clear of worldly conflicts. Must ensure the Elder never hears of this.
